title.narrative: ISS, East Africa Peace and Security Governance Programme (EPSG), 2022 - 2025
ISS, East Africa Peace and Security Governance Programme (EPSG), 2022 - 2025

description.narrative:
The ISS Nairobi Office, through the East African Peace and Security Governance (EPSG) programme, will seek to expand and deepen its strategic presence and engagement in Kenya, Eastern Africa and the Great Lakes region. ISS intends to work with selected governments in East Africa and subregional organizations such as the EAC and ICGLR. The programme "Strengthening regional capacities for conflict prevention, peacebuilding, the rule of law and democratic governance in Eastern Africa (including the Great Lakes)" is focused on contributing to two strategic outcomes:
1. Enhanced knowledge and understanding of threats to peace and security in East Africa and the Great Lakes among relevant regional stakeholders.
2. Improved national and regional cooperative capacities to address threats to peace and security, prevent conflict and enhance community security.
The planned budget is SEK 14 million SEK over three years.

Institute of Security Studies ska genomföra ett projekt för att ”stärka regionala kapaciteter för konfliktförebyggande, fredsbyggande, rättsstatsprincipen och demokratiskt styre i östra Afrika (inklusive Stora Sjö-området)” under perioden december 2022 – november 2025 som en del av deras program för freds- och säkerhetsstyrning i Östafrika. Sidas stöd uppgår till 14,4 miljoner kronor. Projektet syftar till att bidra till två strategiska resultat: 1. Förbättrad kunskap och förståelse för hot mot fred och säkerhet i Östafrika och de stora sjöarna bland relevanta regionala intressenter. 2. Förbättrad nationell och regional samarbetskapacitet för att hantera hot mot fred och säkerhet, förebygga konflikter och förbättra säkerheten i samhället. ISS avser att arbeta med utvalda regeringar i Östafrika och subregionala organisationer som EAC och ICGLR. Tematiska fokusområden är konfliktförebyggande, fredsbyggande, främjande av demokratiskt styre och rättsstatsprincipen.

The Institute of Security Studies will implement a project to “Strengthening regional capacities for conflict prevention, peacebuilding, the rule of law and democratic governance in Eastern Africa (including the Great Lakes region)” for the period December 2022 – November 2025 as part of their East Africa Peace and Security Governance Programme. Sida’s support amounts to SEK 14,4 million SEK. The project aims to contribute towards two strategic outcomes:
1. Enhanced knowledge and understanding of threats to peace and security in East Africa and the Great Lakes among relevant regional stakeholders. 2. Improved national and regional cooperative capacities to address threats to peace and security, prevent conflict and enhance community security.
ISS intends to work with selected governments in East Africa and subregional organizations such as the EAC and ICGLR. Thematic areas of focus are conflict prevention, peacebuilding, promoting democratic governance and rule of law.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative: It is difficult for Sida to assess the results. Few activities have been carried out in which ISS has taken a lead and organised something. In addition, the cooperation with the regional organisations East Africa Community (EAC) and International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) has not, to Sida's knowledge produced any material results. ISS has mentioned the participation in different events organized by the above mentioned REC:s but it is unclear in what capacity ISS participated and how it contributed to the processes. ISS mentioned in the application for grants in 2022 that it has an MoU with EAC and that it will develop a shared workplan. This workplan was still not in place in 2024. Sida can not determine that there were any joint activities between ISS and the RECs for 2023 and 2024. In 2023, the narrative report mentioned consultations with EAC, AU and ICGLR. In 2024, the narrative report mentioned that a workshop was held with EAC on December 15 2024 and an expert seminar with EAC on September 18. The details of the workshop in December has not been elaborated. They were presented as one time events. Furthermore, the narrative report for 2024 mentioned several activities that were not, in the opinion of Sida, related to the fulfillment of the agreed goals. One example of this is advising the Kenyan national security advisor on the deployment of police troops to Haiti. Most of the activities that have been done are in relation to different policy briefs and different policy briefings to diplomats. Sida assesses that the objectives will not be achieved for the above mentioned reasons. The management of the project does not according to Sida's assessment have a clear idea of what shall be done and neither a strategy of implemention. Under these circumstances, it is very hard to produce any meaningful results. Sida has therefore decided not to disburse the last tranch of money and not to extend this project.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
